The Guadagolo Formation (Prenestini Mountains) is a Miocene (Burdigalian-Langhiano) carbonate succession deposited in the transition between the Apulian carbonate platform and the Umbria-Sabina basin.
The Guadagnaolo Formation (Mi, Prenestina Mountains, central Apennines) is deposited on the transition between Latium-Abruzzo Platform and Umbria-Sabina Basin.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the stratigraphic and isotopic record of the Guadagno Fm, deposited in the Mediterranean platform-to-basin transition during the early to middle Miocene, which represents a key area to understand the regional effects of the Monterey event.
the stratigraphic evolution and the paleoenvironmental reconstruction of a carbonate ramp in the Mediterranean basin during the Miocene.
the study of the stratigraphic evolution and the environmental setting of the Guadalgno Fm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(i) The Guadagnol Fm. is the record of a distal outer-ramp environment in the Mediterranean basin; (ii) the Monterey event is recorded in the Central Appenines carbonate ramp; (iii) the Guadagnol Formation is the record of the Monterey carbon isotope excursion, with a weaker signal due to the fractionating effect of the primary producers; (iv) the largest positive carbon isotopic excursion is recorded in a shallower depositional environment.
the Monterey Event is not a unique event but a long-lasting event with different intensities, depending on local and regional conditions.

the Guadagnulo Fm is a stratigraphic record of the Monterey event in a distal ramp environment, where the carbon isotope excursion and its magnitude is controlled by the sponge abundance, and the seawater fertility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

1) the Monterey event was a global phenomenon, 2) it is recorded in the carbonate ramps, 3) it is attenuated in the carbonate ramps and 4) it is related to a regional environmental change, such as the global cooling and the continental erosion.

the Monterey Event in the Central Apennisines carbonate ramps was characterized by a positive carbon isotope excursions with an attenuate signal in the spongolithic member and a larger excursion in the upper member.
the Monterey event in the Central Apennaic carbonate ramps is recorded as an isotope excursion of reduced amplitude compared to the pelagic and platform records.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Monterey event was a global phenomenon, but it is recorded differently depending on the depositional environment.

the Monterey carbon isotope excursion in the Guadagnolu Fm is not as pronounced as in the open marine settings, and it is attenuated due to fractionation effect of the primary producers of the shallow photic zone, and the 12C-en-riched CO2 derived from the oxidation of the sponge organic matter.
the Monterey event was recorded in the Central Mediterranean carbonate ramp, but it has a weaker signal compared to the pelagic and carbonate platform records.
